<h1>Cloud sync setup</h1>

This page connects your Pis to Google Drive with
[rclone](https://rclone.org), so each Pi can back up its sessions and browse
the other's. What the sync does once it is running (the publish projection,
the peer mirror and the read-only peer IO view) is in
[Saving and loading sessions](/documentation/MSEQ/sessions).

You do **not** need to understand the sync daemon to follow this. You do need:

- physical or SSH access to each Pi as the `patch` user,
- a laptop or desktop **with a web browser** (the Pi is headless, so the
  Google sign-in step cannot be done on the Pi alone),
- a Google account for the Pis to share. A dedicated account for your rig is
  better than your personal one, because every Pi will hold a credential for it.

Work through the sections in order. Sections 1 to 3 are done **once**, not per
Pi. Sections 4 to 7 are done **on each Pi**. Section 8 checks that the Pis can
see each other.

> ⚠️ **`/etc/mseq/rclone.conf` is a secret.** It contains a live Google
> credential, and `rclone obscure` only disguises it: it does not encrypt it.
> Never commit the file, paste it into chat or logs, or copy it into the repo.
> If it leaks, go to Google Account → *Security → Third-party access* and
> remove `mseq-cloud-sync`, then repeat Sections 1 and 5.

## 0. Choose how the Pis sign in (read first)

There are two ways for the Pis to sign in to Drive. Pick one before touching
anything.

| | **Shared-account OAuth** (recommended) | **Per-Pi service accounts** |
|---|---|---|
| How | Every Pi signs in *as* the same Google account | Each Pi has its own service-account JSON; the `mseq/` folder is shared with each |
| Peer browse | Works with no extra sharing (both Pis are the same Drive identity) | Requires explicitly sharing `mseq/` with each service account |
| Blast radius if a Pi is stolen | Full access to the Google account | Only the `mseq/` tree that account was shared into |
| Setup effort | Lower | Higher |

If you trust everyone who can get their hands on the Pis, **use shared-account
OAuth.** The rest of this page is written for that path. The service-account
variant is summarised in Section 9.

---

## 1. Create your own Google OAuth client (once)

rclone ships with a *shared* default OAuth client ID. It works, but it is
**heavily rate-limited** and you will hit throttling during normal sync. Create
your own client. It is free and takes ~10 minutes.

Do this once, signed in to the **Google account the Pis will share**, at
<https://console.cloud.google.com>.

1. **Create a project** (top bar → project picker → *New Project*). Name it
   e.g. `mseq-cloud-sync`. Select it once created.

2. **Enable the Drive API**: *APIs & Services → Library →* search "Google Drive
   API" → **Enable**.

3. **Configure the OAuth consent screen**: *APIs & Services → OAuth consent
   screen*.
   - User type: **External**.
   - Fill in the required app name (`mseq-cloud-sync`), the support email, and
     the developer email. You can leave logos/links blank.
   - **Scopes**: you can leave the scope list empty here; rclone requests the
     scope at config time (Section 5). Click through.
   - **Test users**: **add the shared account as a test user.** This is
     important (see the box below).

   > ⚠️ **Publishing status = "Testing" expires tokens after 7 days.** If you
   > leave the consent screen in *Testing* status, the refresh token Google
   > issues will stop working after 7 days and sync will silently die. Two
   > fixes: (a) add the account as a **Test User** *and* accept that you may
   > need to re-auth periodically, or (b) click **Publish App** (push to
   > *Production*): for an unverified app used only by its own account this is
   > fine and gives a non-expiring refresh token. **Recommended: Publish App.**

4. **Create the OAuth client credential**: *APIs & Services → Credentials →
   Create Credentials → OAuth client ID*.
   - Application type: **Desktop app**.
   - Name: `mseq-rclone`.
   - Click **Create**. Google shows a **Client ID** and **Client secret**.
     Copy both somewhere safe (a password manager). You'll paste them into
     `rclone config` on each Pi in Section 5.

---

## 2. (Reference) The shared Drive layout

The sync daemon expects this tree in the shared account's Drive, with one
folder per Pi named after its hostname. The examples on this page call the two
Pis `mseq-a` and `mseq-b`. You don't create the per-Pi folders by hand: the
smoke test in Section 7 and the daemon's first push create them. You only
create the **root** in Section 3.

```
mseq/
  mseq-a/
    patches/        # mseq-a's published sessions (it writes; its peer reads)
    _contrib/       # reserved; nothing uses it yet
  mseq-b/
    patches/        # mseq-b's published sessions
    _contrib/
```

---

## 3. Create the shared root folder (once)

The `mseq/` folder must exist before either Pi pushes. Easiest: in the Drive
web UI, signed in as the shared account, create a top-level folder
named exactly **`mseq`**. That's all this step needs.

(You can also create it with rclone from any machine once you've completed a
config: `rclone --config <conf> mkdir gdrive:mseq`.)

---

## 4. Install rclone on the Pi

On each Pi, as `patch`:

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y rclone
```

Create the secrets directory. It must be writable by the `patch` group because
rclone refreshes OAuth tokens by writing a temporary config file beside
`/etc/mseq/rclone.conf` and renaming it into place:

```bash
sudo install -d -m 0770 -o root -g patch /etc/mseq
```

---

## 5. Run `rclone config` for Google Drive (on each Pi: the headless flow)

This is the step people get stuck on, because the Pi has **no browser** and
rclone's default flow tries to open one. Follow the wizard answers exactly.

On the Pi:

```bash
umask 077
rclone config --config /tmp/mseq-rclone.conf
```

Answer the wizard:

| Prompt | Answer |
|---|---|
| `n/s/q` | **`n`** (new remote) |
| `name>` | **`gdrive`** |
| `Storage>` | **`drive`** (type it, or the number for "Google Drive") |
| `client_id>` | paste the **Client ID** from Section 1 |
| `client_secret>` | paste the **Client secret** from Section 1 |
| `scope>` | **`1`** = `drive` (full access). **Do not** pick `drive.file` (see the scope note below). |
| `service_account_file>` | leave **blank** (shared-account OAuth; press Enter) |
| `Edit advanced config?` | **`n`** |
| `Use auto config?` | **`n`** ← **critical on a headless Pi** |

After you answer **No** to "Use auto config?", rclone prints a command like:

```
rclone authorize "drive" "<long-base64-blob>"
```

Now go to your **laptop/desktop that has rclone installed and a browser**, and
run that exact command there:

```bash
# On your desktop, NOT the Pi:
rclone authorize "drive" "<long-base64-blob>"
```

It opens a browser, you sign in as the shared account and approve
access. rclone then prints a token blob (`{"access_token":...}`). Copy the
**entire** blob, return to the Pi's still-waiting wizard, and paste it at the
`config_token>` prompt.

Finish the wizard:

| Prompt | Answer |
|---|---|
| `Configure this as a Shared Drive (Team Drive)?` | **`n`** (the shared account's Drive is a normal My Drive, not a Team Drive) |
| `y/e/d` (confirm remote) | **`y`** |
| `e/n/d/r/c/s/q` | **`q`** (quit config) |

> 💡 **No desktop rclone?** Two alternatives to the `rclone authorize` dance:
> install rclone on the desktop (it's a single binary), **or** SSH into the Pi
> with a forwarded port: `ssh -L 53682:localhost:53682 patch@<pi>.local`,
> and then answer **`y`** to "Use auto config?"; the browser on your laptop
> will reach the Pi's local callback through the tunnel.

### Scope note (why `drive`, not `drive.file`)

It is tempting to narrow the token "to the `mseq/` subtree". Be aware:

- OAuth **scopes** are not folder scoping. `drive.file` only lets rclone see
  files *it created*, which **breaks peer browse**: the other Pi could never
  read your published sessions. Use the full **`drive`** scope.
- If you want to reduce blast radius, use rclone's **`root_folder_id`** instead
  (Section 6). That constrains what the *remote* can see, but it is a
  convenience boundary, **not** a security boundary: the token still has
  account-wide reach.

---

## 6. (Optional) Confine the remote to the `mseq/` folder

You can make the `gdrive` remote treat the `mseq/` folder as its root, so a
stray command can't wander the whole Drive. Get the folder's ID from its Drive
URL (`https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<THIS_PART>`), then, on the Pi,
before installing the config:

```bash
rclone config --config /tmp/mseq-rclone.conf
# e (edit existing) → gdrive → walk to advanced config → set:
#   root_folder_id> <THIS_PART>
```

If you set this, the daemon has to address paths **relative to `mseq/`** (for
example `gdrive:mseq-a/patches` rather than `gdrive:mseq/mseq-a/patches`). To
avoid confusion across the two Pis, it's simplest to **skip `root_folder_id`**
and keep the full `gdrive:mseq/...` paths that `RCLONE_REMOTE` in Section 7
assumes. Reduce blast radius with file permissions and physical trust instead.

---

## 7. Install the config and smoke-test (on each Pi)

Move the freshly-built config into place with permissions that let the daemon
user refresh OAuth tokens. rclone may rewrite the config after a successful
command, so the file itself and the parent `/etc/mseq` directory must be writable
by `patch`:

```bash
sudo install -m 0660 -o patch -g patch /tmp/mseq-rclone.conf /etc/mseq/rclone.conf
rm -f /tmp/mseq-rclone.conf   # /tmp is tmpfs (RAM-backed) on Pi OS
```

If you previously installed the config as `0640 root:patch`, fix it with:

```bash
sudo chown root:patch /etc/mseq
sudo chmod 0770 /etc/mseq
sudo chown patch:patch /etc/mseq/rclone.conf
sudo chmod 0660 /etc/mseq/rclone.conf
```

Without this, `rclone lsd ...` may still list successfully but print errors like
`Failed to save config ... permission denied` whenever it tries to persist a
refreshed token.

Smoke-test **as the daemon user**, always passing the explicit config path:

```bash
sudo -u patch rclone --config /etc/mseq/rclone.conf lsd gdrive:
sudo -u patch rclone --config /etc/mseq/rclone.conf lsd gdrive:mseq
sudo -u patch rclone --config /etc/mseq/rclone.conf mkdir gdrive:mseq/$(hostname)/patches
sudo -u patch rclone --config /etc/mseq/rclone.conf mkdir gdrive:mseq/$(hostname)/_contrib
```

The first two should list without error; the `mkdir`s create this Pi's
folder. (`$(hostname)` is the Pi's `PI_ID`, for example `mseq-a`.)

Then create `/etc/mseq/cloud-sync.env`. All six fields are required: the sync
daemon refuses to run without them, and omitting `PATCHES_DIR` gets you
`PATCHES_DIR: unbound variable` on the first cycle rather than a helpful error:

```sh
# /etc/mseq/cloud-sync.env: this Pi's cloud-sync identity
PI_ID=mseq-a                         # this Pi's id (its hostname); names its folder on the remote
PEERS=mseq-b                         # the one peer to mirror from (exactly one, no commas)
RCLONE_REMOTE=gdrive:mseq            # the shared root folder from section 3
RCLONE_CONFIG=/etc/mseq/rclone.conf  # the config installed above
PATCHES_DIR=/home/patch/code/sequencer/patches       # PD's session catalog, the publish source
CLOUD_SYNC_DIR=/home/patch/code/sequencer/cloud-sync
```

`install/cloud-sync.env.example` is the same set with fuller comments, so
copying that and editing `PI_ID` / `PEERS` is the safer route.

Install it `0640 root:patch`:

```bash
sudo chown root:patch /etc/mseq/cloud-sync.env
sudo chmod 0640 /etc/mseq/cloud-sync.env
```

### 7.1 Verify the `cloud-sync/publish` tmpfs

The sync daemon publishes from a generated projection under
`cloud-sync/publish/`, not directly from `patches/`. That publish directory has
to be a tmpfs mount so the daemon's temporary generations do not add SD-card
write load.

You do not provision it here. `install/bootstrap-pi.sh` installs and enables a
system-scope mount unit for exactly this path, and `mseq-cloud-sync.service`
depends on it via `RequiresMountsFor=`. **Do not also add an `/etc/fstab` entry.**
Two definitions of one mountpoint is a drift generator, and the unit is the one
the service waits on.

So this step is a check. Run on **each Pi**:

```bash
findmnt /home/patch/code/sequencer/cloud-sync/publish
systemctl is-enabled 'home-patch-code-sequencer-cloud\x2dsync-publish.mount'
```

`findmnt` should show `FSTYPE` as `tmpfs` with options similar to
`size=20480k,mode=750,uid=1000,gid=1000`, and the unit should report `enabled`.
If both are as expected, move on to section 7.2.

**If the mount is missing**, the bootstrap step did not run (or the unit was
removed). Reinstall it from the repo rather than reaching for fstab:

```bash
cd /home/patch/code/sequencer
MOUNT_UNIT='home-patch-code-sequencer-cloud\x2dsync-publish.mount'
sudo mkdir -p cloud-sync/publish
sudo chown patch:patch cloud-sync cloud-sync/publish
sudo install -m 0644 "install/systemd/system/$MOUNT_UNIT" "/etc/systemd/system/$MOUNT_UNIT"
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now "$MOUNT_UNIT"
findmnt /home/patch/code/sequencer/cloud-sync/publish
```

**If an old fstab entry is present**, remove it. It duplicates the unit, and a
line split across two lines makes `mount` fail with a parse error such as
`parse error at line 7`:

```bash
sudo cp /etc/fstab /etc/fstab.bak.mseq-cloud-sync.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
sudo python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

path = Path('/etc/fstab')
lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
fixed = []
skip_orphan_zero = False
for line in lines:
    if '/home/patch/code/sequencer/cloud-sync/publish' in line:
        skip_orphan_zero = True
        continue
    if skip_orphan_zero and line.strip() == '0':
        skip_orphan_zero = False
        continue
    skip_orphan_zero = False
    fixed.append(line.rstrip())
path.write_text('\n'.join(fixed) + '\n')
PY
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
findmnt /home/patch/code/sequencer/cloud-sync/publish
```

### 7.2 Final per-Pi permission and mount check

Run this on each Pi before moving on:

```bash
stat -c 'etc_mseq=%U:%G %a' /etc/mseq
stat -c 'rclone_conf=%U:%G %a' /etc/mseq/rclone.conf
stat -c 'cloud_sync_env=%U:%G %a' /etc/mseq/cloud-sync.env
findmnt -no TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS /home/patch/code/sequencer/cloud-sync/publish
sudo -u patch rclone --config /etc/mseq/rclone.conf lsd gdrive:mseq
```

Expected state:

```text
etc_mseq=root:patch 770
rclone_conf=patch:patch 660
cloud_sync_env=root:patch 640
/home/patch/code/sequencer/cloud-sync/publish tmpfs ...
```

The final rclone command should not print `Failed to save config`.

---

## 8. Confirm the Pis can see each other (after both are set up)

If this is wrong, the peer IO view just looks empty, with no obvious error.
From **each** Pi, list the **other** Pi's published folder:

```bash
# On mseq-a:
sudo -u patch rclone --config /etc/mseq/rclone.conf lsd gdrive:mseq/mseq-b/patches
# On mseq-b:
sudo -u patch rclone --config /etc/mseq/rclone.conf lsd gdrive:mseq/mseq-a/patches
```

An **empty but successful** listing (the peer hasn't pushed yet) is fine. A
**permission or not-found error** means the sign-in model isn't wired
correctly. Fix it before expecting the peer IO view to show anything.

---

## 9. Service-account variant (only if you chose it in Section 0)

Instead of signing in through the browser:

1. In Cloud Console: *IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Create*. Create one
   service account **per Pi** (or one shared: your call). For each, *Keys → Add
   Key → JSON* and download the JSON.
2. Copy each Pi's JSON to it as `/etc/mseq/google-service-account.json`
   (`0640 root:patch`).
3. In `rclone config`, leave `client_id`/`client_secret` blank and set
   `service_account_file> /etc/mseq/google-service-account.json`.
4. **Share `mseq/` with each service account's email** (it looks like
   `name@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) as **Editor** in the Drive web UI.
   Without this, the service account cannot read or write the shared tree.
5. Run the Section 8 check.

If a service-account JSON leaks, delete that key in Cloud Console
(*IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Keys*) and add a new one.
